entry_point: agent tool execution through the Feishu plugin's registered tools, via the plugin registration API (registerTool): feishu_doc, feishu_app_scopes, feishu_wiki, feishu_drive, feishu_perm, feishu_chat and the feishu_bitable_* tools

verified.entry_point: Every case drives the real registered tool through a harness that implements the plugin registration API (the same seam the project's own tests use); the Feishu client factory is replaced with a recording proxy so a test can observe which account's credentials are used and whether any Feishu API call happened. Each security test fails on the pinned+injected tree and passes on the reference fix; each functional test passes on both.
sites: extensions/feishu/src/tool-account.ts:16-49 (implicit account selection: no account chosen must still select an account that allows the family) and :51-71 (the shared resolver every tool uses) — the published-fix landing point
extensions/feishu/src/docx.ts:1386-1396 (feishu_doc: client plus the media-size resolver call) — published-fix site
extensions/feishu/src/docx.ts:1587 (feishu_app_scopes reusing the document module's client helper) — published-fix far site with its own tool family
extensions/feishu/src/chat.ts:133-168 (hand-rolled per-request account selection for the chat tool) — injected sibling
extensions/feishu/src/bitable.ts:635-641,818-838 (bulk record import with its own long-timeout client, bypassing the module's gated helper) — injected sibling
routes: A request naming a documents-off account (explicit accountId over an allowed session account) still read and wrote documents on the pinned tree: confirmed with a recording client (client.docx.documentBlock.list with the disabled account's app id).
The app-scope diagnostic ran on an account with the diagnostic off while documents were on: confirmed (client.application.scope.list).
An account that never mentions a family that defaults to off (permissions) still ran permission operations: confirmed (client.drive.permissionMember.list).
A request naming no account ran under the first-listed account while that account had the family off and another account had it on: confirmed (client.wiki.space.list).
chat, with the injected per-request selection, ran chat lookups on an account with chat off: confirmed (client.im.chat.get).
the injected bulk Bitable import ran on an account with Bitable off: confirmed (client.bitable.appTableRecord.batchCreate).

Dismissed, not built: the channel plugin's message actions (channel-info / member-info) call chat read APIs for the session account without a tools.chat check. They are governed by the channel action settings, not by the per-account tool families; the property read literally does not map them, so no test uses them.
injected_siblings: extensions/feishu/src/chat.ts: the chat tool resolves its own account from the request (resolveFeishuRuntimeAccount + createFeishuClient) instead of the shared tool resolver, so no family gate is applied. Our copy only.
extensions/feishu/src/bitable.ts: a bulk record import tool builds its own long-timeout client from resolveFeishuRuntimeAccount, next to the module's already-gated helper. Our copy only.
verified.services: none; the image installs the whole pnpm workspace at build time, grading is offline
verified.project_tests_run: extensions/feishu/src/{tool-account-routing,docx.account-selection,chat}.test.ts (25 tests) plus the eleven hidden functional tests (36 in total), all passing on the pinned+injected tree and on the reference fix with Node 22; the project test files are re-run as part of the functional group from the verifier image's pristine copies. The project test files that replace the shared tool-account module with a fixed export map (drive, bitable, wiki) and the one that calls the shared resolver without a family (tool-account.test.ts) are deliberately not in the functional group: a valid fix that adds a new shared helper, or makes the family a required argument as upstream later did, would fail them for a reason the report never states.

wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: the guarded decision has no role, peer or direction axis; it is which account runs the operation, and every account is exercised in both the allowed and the refused direction.
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the guarded value is the resolved account identity; a correct fix always evaluates the same account that the client is built from, and there is no normalising or adjusting step that could change the value between the check and the sink.
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: the account identity is normalised by the product before any fix sees it, so a correct guard cannot be fooled by a differently spelled account id; no test relies on a spelling variant.
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: the decision is read from local account configuration, not from an external authority whose empty answer could fail the check open; an account with no configuration still gets the product's defaults, which the guard applies.

traps.lever: base flaw: the per-account family setting is applied only when tools are announced, never when an operation runs; and a request that names no account must re-select an allowed one instead of being refused
traps.shape: a tool executes with an account whose own effective configuration disables the tool family, however the account was chosen
traps.reason_to_dismiss: once an account is resolved, refusing it when it is not allowed looks like the whole fix; the unnamed-account case reads as "use the operator's default account", so a refusal there is not seen as a regression
